About This Job
The Role
• Understand and build effective and efficient schedules around our clients and Care Professionals.
• Ensure schedules are prepared, considering travel time, holidays, training and last-minute cancellations.
• Be responsive to changes in the schedule and liaise with relevant team members.
• Match Care Professionals to new clients in conjunction with client services team and arrange introductions.
• Ensure client schedules are matched to their needs, with the same Care Professional and the same times each week, where possible.
• Develop excellent relationships with both clients and Care Professionals so both can enjoy positive experiences.
• Work with the recruitment and Managers to ensure sufficient current and future staffing levels are met.
• Work with the Care Team to ensure new and existing care packages can be resourced and scheduled on a timely basis.
• Add and maintain all client and Care Professional information onto to the electronic scheduling system.
• Carry out any other duties deemed necessary for the successful operation of the business.
• Ensure compliance with Home Instead’s Equality, Diversity and Equal Opportunities Policy, in respect of employment and service delivery.
Essential Criteria
• Experience of working in a scheduling role within a home care or other relevant environment such as logistics.
• Good working knowledge of IT systems with experience of Microsoft Office or Google Suite and CRM software with the ability to learn and adopt new technologies where appropriate.
• Highly resilient and positive with excellent communications skills.
• Excellent organisation and prioritisation skills with the ability to work calmly and accurately under pressure.
• Team player with strong interpersonal skills with the ability to build rapport quickly.
• Excellent attention to detail with the ability to multi-task.
• Logical and analytical with the ability to work on own initiative and meet deadlines.

Additional Information
If you have a passion for caring and the motivation to help us achieve our ambitions, we would love to hear from you.
We encourage applications from all sections of the community as we want to reflect the neighbourhoods in which we work. Home Instead is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of adults and expects all staff to share this commitment. This role is subject to DBS enhanced disclosure.

About This Job
Are you looking for a meaningful way to connect with your community?  We have an exciting opportunity for a new care assistant to join our 'Outstanding' island team. If you're looking for some extra weekend or evening work, this could be the perfect position for you!
Where no two visits are the same, daily tasks can include:
Assisting with personal care:
• Provide medication reminders
• Help with bathing, dressing and grooming
• Help with continence care
• Assist to eat and drink
Home help:
• Run errands / collect prescriptions etc
• Performing light housekeeping tasks (dusting, vacuuming, making beds, changing linens, cleaning bathrooms, kitchens, washing and ironing, taking out rubbish, caring for houseplants etc.)
• Organise and tidy cupboards and check food expiry dates
• Plan prepare and tidy away meals
• Answer the door
• Assist with pet care
• Provide Dementia / Alzheimer care
• Provide respite / convalescence care
• Assist with morning/wake up and or evening/tuck in
Companionship:
• Offer companionship and conversation
• Monitor diet and eating
• Stimulate and encourage through a variety of activities (for example clothing selection, hobbies and crafts)
• Arrange and provide reminders for appointments, activities and outings

Does this sound like the role for you?

About This Job
This is a key customer-facing role focused on building strong relationships with external customers while providing support with quotations and technical specifications. You will play an important part in delivering a high standard of service, ensuring customer enquiries are handled efficiently and accurately across a global customer base.
Reporting to the Customer Service Team Leader, you will work closely with External Sales Teams and the Service Department, acting as a vital link between customers and internal stakeholders to ensure a seamless customer experience.
In this role, you will be responsible for processing quotations accurately and within agreed timescales, maintaining departmental KPIs and service standards. You will review technical documentation, specifications, and customer purchase orders before contracts are issued, ensuring accuracy and attention to detail throughout. You will also respond to customer enquiries promptly, providing a professional and customer-focused service at every stage.
This opportunity would suit someone with customer service experience who is looking to develop their career within a technical sales environment and gain exposure to a broad range of technical and commercial activities.

Qualifications
Experience Requirements:
• Experience of working within ERP Systems
• Experience of dealing with quotations.
• Able to provide exceptional customer service.
• Strong communication skills.
The Successful Candidate:
• Has a proactive and positive approach.
• Communicates effectively at all levels.
• Demonstrates excellent accuracy and attention to detail.
• Builds strong relationships with customers and colleagues.
• Takes ownership and delivers a high standard of service.
• Is keen to develop a career within a technical sales environment.

Additional Information
Rotork is the market-leading global flow control and instrumentation company, helping our customers manage the flow or liquids, gases and powders across many industries worldwide.
Our purpose is Keeping the World Flowing for Future Generations.
For over sixty years, the world has relied on us to create the things that keep everything moving.
From oil and gas to water and shipping, pharmaceuticals and food- these are the flows on which our modern world depends.
Today we're respected and admired for our people, performance and products. Our success flows from our commitment to engineering excellence, and that's what we will always pursue, safely and sustainably.
Rotork is going through an exciting period of change and growth, building on our existing market leadership. It's a great time to join us and make an impact in shaping the future of our business.

About This Job
Why Start Your Career at S&W?
Starting your career is about more than just a job. It's about the people you learn from, the relationships you build and the experiences that shape you. Whether that's passing an exam, achieving a personal milestone or celebrating success with your colleagues, you'll be part of a team that's invested in your growth, celebrates your achievements and supports you to be yourself.
At S&W, you'll be given meaningful responsibility from the start, alongside the support and guidance needed to help you succeed. You'll learn from experienced colleagues, develop valuable professional skills and build confidence as your career progresses.
As one of the UK's fastest-growing accountancy and advisory firms, we offer a balance of opportunity and support. You'll learn from people at every level of the business, gain exposure to a variety of clients, industries and experiences, and develop the skills, knowledge and confidence needed to build a successful career.
No previous experience in accountancy, finance or professional services is required. We're looking for people with the right attitude and potential to succeed. If you're curious, eager to learn and ready to challenge yourself, we'll provide the training, support and opportunities to help you make the most of your potential.
The Private Client Tax team at S&W
Our Private Client Tax Services team works with a wide range of individuals, families and business owners, helping them navigate important decisions and manage their tax affairs with confidence. With over 6,000 private clients and 1,500 trusts, you'll gain experience supporting everyone from entrepreneurs and family businesses to high-net-worth individuals and families.
As part of the team, you'll help clients meet their tax obligations, communicate with HMRC and support them with their financial goals. You'll learn how to prepare tax returns and calculations, research solutions to complex problems and assist in delivering tailored advice. Along the way, you'll develop valuable technical, analytical and client-facing skills while building trusted relationships and making a real difference to the people and businesses you work with.
What will you be doing?
As part of our Private Client Tax team, you'll gain hands-on experience supporting a wide range of clients with their tax affairs and financial planning. This could include helping clients identify tax-efficient strategies, preparing tax returns and calculations, liaising with HMRC and supporting the delivery of tailored advice.
You'll be given responsibility from an early stage in your career, with the opportunity to build strong client relationships and develop your professional confidence. As your experience grows, you'll take on more ownership of client work, support new trainees joining the team and contribute to a variety of projects. Depending on the work available, this could include reviewing financial controls, supporting due diligence assignments and helping clients navigate more complex tax matters.
Alongside your day-to-day role, you'll study towards the ATT and CTA qualifications, as well as a government-recognised Level 7 professional qualification. You'll begin building the technical knowledge that underpins your work while developing the commercial, analytical and people skills needed for a successful career in professional services. With dedicated study support, expert tuition and guidance from colleagues who have completed the same journey, you'll have the support and resources to succeed throughout your training contract.
Your work will include:
• Liaising with clients and third parties to obtain information and build an understanding of their circumstances and objectives.
• Preparing tax returns and repayment claims, ensuring clients meet their compliance obligations accurately and on time.
• Helping clients understand their upcoming tax liabilities and the tax matters that may affect them.
• Assisting with the preparation of client advice, including technical tax research, strategic planning and drafting reports and recommendations.
• Corresponding with clients, HMRC and other third parties by phone, email and letter to support the delivery of high-quality client service.
To Be Successful in This Role
You'll be someone who:
• Is curious, eager to learn and open to new challenges
• Enjoys working with others and building positive relationships
• Has a keen eye for detail and enjoys solving problems
• Is proactive and looks for ways to make a positive contribution
• Takes ownership of their development and is motivated to achieve their goals
You'll also need to:
• Be committed to working towards the Level 7 ATT/CTA Tax Pathway professional qualification
• A Level: Predicted or obtained minimum 112 UCAS points in top three A Levels (or equivalent), excluding General Studies
• GCSE: Minimum Grade 5 (or equivalent), in English Language and Maths
No previous experience in accountancy, finance or professional services is required.
Your Learning & Development
We'll support you throughout your qualification journey with a leading UK training provider, dedicated study time and practical experience that complements your learning.
You'll join as part of a cohort and benefit from a strong support network that includes experienced colleagues, a buddy and our Learning & Development team. From your first day, you'll have people around you to guide you, answer questions and help you make the most of every opportunity.
As a Colleague at S&W, You'll Have Access to Benefits That Include
• Fully funded training towards professional qualifications
• Competitive salary
• Private medical insurance
• Life assurance
• Pension contribution
• Generous holiday package
• Option to purchase additional holiday
• Cycle to work scheme
• Season ticket loan
• Eye care support
• Shared parental leave
Our Commitment to Inclusion
We are proud to value the differences that a diverse workforce brings, representative of society and our clients. At S&W we have a wide range of highly active employee resource groups and we’re delivering multiple diversity, equity and inclusion initiatives across the organisation. It is our commitment to provide a workspace where all colleagues, regardless of identity, background, or circumstance, feel respected as individuals and feel that they can achieve their full potential and work in a safe, supportive, and inclusive environment.
We are happy to make any reasonable adjustments to accommodate for your needs throughout the application process. Please let your Recruiter know.

jobs.smartrecruiters.com/frpadvisory/744.description_excerpt:
About This Job
Role Overview
This role sits within FRP's Forensic Services team in Belfast and focuses on delivering forensic accounting services in relation to personal injury matters. Working closely with solicitors, insurers, counsel and other stakeholders, you will manage engagements involving the quantification of financial losses and support clients through complex claims and disputes. You will also play an important role in developing junior team members and supporting the continued growth of FRP's Forensic Services practice.
Key Responsibilities
• Manage a portfolio of personal injury forensic accounting engagements, acting as the primary contact for solicitors, insurers, counsel, and other stakeholders.
• Prepare and review financial loss calculations, including loss of earnings, business losses, pension losses, care claims, and dependency claims.
• Analyse financial, employment, business, and tax records to quantify past and future economic losses.
• Identify key quantum issues, determine information requirements, and assess supporting evidence.
• Assist in developing case strategy and advising on approaches to loss quantification.
• Prepare and review expert reports, schedules of loss, joint statements, and critiques of opposing expert evidence.
• Support expert witness assignments, including conferences with counsel, mediations, and court proceedings where required.
• Manage case deadlines, budgets, and resource requirements, ensuring efficient delivery of engagements.
• Review and supervise the work of junior team members, providing coaching and technical guidance.
• Contribute to practice development through business development, client relationship management, training, and continuous improvement initiatives.
• Take a leading role in the development and growth of the personal injury practice, identifying opportunities to expand client relationships, enhance service offerings, and strengthen the firm's market presence within the personal injury sector.

Qualifications
Essential
• ACA, ACCA or equivalent professional qualification
• Experience within forensic accounting, disputes, expert witness or personal injury-related work
• Strong analytical and financial modelling skills
• Experience reviewing complex financial information and producing high-quality written reports
• Strong communication and stakeholder management skills
• Ability to manage multiple engagements and competing deadlines
• Experience supervising, mentoring or reviewing the work of others
Desirable
• Experience preparing expert reports, schedules of loss or joint statements
• Experience working with solicitors, insurers, counsel or other legal professionals
• Knowledge of personal injury, clinical negligence or fatal accident claims
• Expert witness training or other relevant specialist qualifications

Additional Information
Our Values
• Straightforward: We provide clear, no-nonsense advice
• Confident: Our guidance is backed by expertise and evidence
• Pragmatic: We focus on practical solutions and tangible outcomes
• Real: We are professional yet approachable, understanding the challenges our clients face
Our Commitment to You and the Environment
At FRP Advisory Group, sustainability is integral to our strategy and operations. Our sustainability depends on building and maintaining meaningful, long-term relationships with all our stakeholders - including our employees, clients, and local communities - while also reducing our impact on the natural environment.
We are always striving to improve in all areas - whether it’s our people, our clients, our planet or our governance. Our ongoing success as a business depends on our sustainability and agility in a changing and challenging global landscape.
We are committed to fostering an inclusive, equitable, and diverse culture for our people. We maintain an Equal Opportunities Policy, ensuring that recruitment and employment decisions are based solely on the skills and experience required for our professional services - regardless of ethnicity, race, sexual orientation, disability, or any other protected characteristic. We believe every individual should have the opportunity to thrive.
Our learning and development programmes enable us to invest in growing our employees’ careers. We aim to empower our team members to each achieve their potential.
We are committed to growing long-term relationships with our clients and supporting them in achieving their objectives. We understand that our clients’ sustainability and success lead to our sustainability and success. We are emotionally invested in our clients right from the beginning.

About This Job
Join the team redefining how the world experiences design.
Hey, g'day, mabuhay, kia ora, 你好, hallo, vítejte!
Thanks for stopping by. We know job ads can feel a bit formulaic sometimes, but we promise Canva is anything but. If you're drawn to what we're building and you see yourself in this role, we'd love to hear from you.
Where and How You Can Work
Our London office is a hub for collaboration and energy. But we also believe in working where you do your best thinking. This role is based in London, with the flexibility to work in a way that suits you.
Canva's mission is to empower the world to design. With 285+ million monthly active users across 190+ countries, we're building the world's most loved visual communication platform. We're not a template tool. We're an AI-powered visual work platform that's replacing legacy tools across design, documents, presentations, video, and websites.
About the role:
• This is not an operations role, and it is not a "run the playbook" role. We're looking for a strategist who will figure out what the playbook should be.
• You'll sit on the International Supergroup Leadership Team (SGL) and work directly with the Head of International to answer two questions. Top-down: how should we segment our markets and allocate investment across them? Bottom-up: what causally drives growth in each market, and how do we make it repeatable? International is accountable for both MAU and ARR.
• In this role you'll form hypotheses, follow hunches, place bold bets, and validate with data. You'll partner closely with the Data Lead, Finance Lead, Leadership Operations, Country Managers, and central product, content and marketing teams. The team is globally distributed: leadership across Sydney, Europe and Dubai time zones, specialties in Sydney, and teams in every market, which gives this role real autonomy.
What you'll do:
Portfolio Strategy (Top-Down):
• Segment the 23 Pioneer markets by penetration, maturity and competitive landscape, and decide how our playbook should differ: one playbook with modules maximised per market, or different playbooks for different clusters.
• Shape investment allocation. Partner with Finance to build the principles for deploying headcount, contingent workers and marketing budget across the portfolio, and feed the monthly MBR conversation.
• Pressure-test market and vertical bets. Invest more in some countries to grow them faster while doing product-only work in others. Build the cases and make the calls with the Head of International.
Growth Drivers & Funnel Excellence (Bottom-Up)
• Find the causal growth drivers. Go beyond correlation to identify what genuinely drives each stage of the funnel in each market, across product-led growth and product distribution, working hand in hand with the International Data Lead.
• Diagnose and tighten the funnel. Analyse why the same product produces 20% 7-day activation in one market and 35% in another, isolate the causes (content, localisation, payments, channels), and turn them into prescriptive plays countries can run.
• Crystallise what you find into repeatable playbooks. You don't have to write every playbook, but you identify the causalities so they become repeatable by the countries.
Scaling What Works Across Markets
• Work with Country Managers and develop growth hunches with them, validate what's working locally, and make it scalable. Retention and reactivation playbooks for markets like Brazil are the first proving ground.
• Live in exploration mode. Form hypotheses, follow hunches, place bold bets, and validate with data. Win buy-in from stakeholders through evidence rather than authority.
You're a match if you have:
• Exceptional analytical skills. You structure ambiguous problems, separate causality from correlation, and draw conclusions others miss.
• Proven growth strategy experience at a consumer technology or digital platform company, with results you can personally attribute. You can articulate a clean growth thesis backed by data, not just intuition.
• Comfort with ambiguity. You are energised by open questions, form a hunch, pursue it, and course-correct fast.
• Genuine growth instinct. You understand funnels end to end, from acquisition and activation through to monetisation and retention, and you bring strong user intuition to match the data.
• Strategic range. You can zoom out to portfolio-level allocation questions and zoom in to why one market's activation rate breaks.
• Data-led decision maker with a strong experimentation mindset. You don't rely on gut alone: you test, measure, and iterate.
• Bold, with bias to action. You place bets, hustle to validate them, and would rather be proven wrong fast than right slowly.
• Exceptional stakeholder craft. You align Country Managers, Finance and central teams behind your recommendations, and you're comfortable operating in a matrix organisation with distributed authority.
• Intellectually honest and first-principles driven. You say what the data says, flag problems early, deconstruct problems from the ground up rather than copy-pasting playbooks, and can articulate why a strategy should work in a specific market.
Highly valued:
• Experience across international or multi-market environments, where the same product behaves differently by market.
• Depth in monetisation and conversion (pricing, payments, upgrade flows), given the ARR side of the mandate.
• Hands-on experience with causal inference and experiment design.
• Genuine familiarity with Canva as a product. We expect you to have used it, not just researched it for the interview.
Canva is a force for good. We believe in empowering everyone to design. We're building a company where the best people want to do their best work. If you're the kind of strategist who gets energised by open questions and wants your analysis to move real markets, we'd love to hear from you.

About This Job
In Custody Careers Advisor (CIAG)
Salary:  £27,800
Location: HMP Kirklevington Grange
We’re looking for a dedicated Careers Information Advice and Guidance Advisor to join our team - a crucial role in supporting individuals inside a custodial setting by providing tailored career advice, guidance, and support. This role aims to empower prisoners to identify their career aspirations, develop their skills, and leverage their strengths to prepare for successful reintegration into society upon release.
About the Role:
You will provide tailored careers advice and guidance to prisoners through both one-to-one sessions and group workshops. You will create and manage personalised learning plans to help prisoners to identify and work towards their goals during custody and in preparation for release. Your role will support rehabilitation by equipping individuals with the skills, qualifications, and opportunities needed to secure employment or further training upon release.
You will organise opportunities for prisoners to connect with employers and participate in employment related activities. Through your support, prisoners will be encouraged to take meaningful steps towards long-term career development and positive reintegration into the community.
This is a demanding yet deeply rewarding role. You'll be working in a challenging environment with individuals who have complex needs and may be hesitant to engage. However, when you help someone break the cycle and take real steps towards transforming their life, the impact is truly life-changing—for them and for you.
What You'll Be Doing:
• Caseload management: Conduct one-to-one assessments to identify prisoners’ skills, career aspirations and training needs and develop a Prisoner Learning Plan (PLP) and effectively manage your caseload to achieve sustained employment, training, education and completion of prison employment outcomes.
• Facilitation: Delivery of engaging sessions to groups of participants around topics such as employability skills, career planning and effective disclosure. Ensuring that goals are realistic and consider any barriers to employment sectors due to the nature of certain types of convictions.
• Relationship Building: Foster genuine, trusting, and non-judgemental relationships with participants creating a safe space for personal growth.
• Stakeholder management: Engage with prison education departments, training providers, employers and probation services to create employment pathways.
• Quality Recording: Work towards agreed KPIs, targets, ensuring quality assurance standards in accordance with the service provider are met.

Qualifications
What We are Looking For:
• Experience delivering guidance, support or advisory services to individuals
• Ability to assess individual needs and develop action plans to support progression
• Experience of managing a caseload and working towards agreed targets or outcomes
• Strong communication skills, with the ability to engage, motivate and influence a diverse range of individuals
• Experience of working with individuals facing barriers to employment or education
• Good organisational skills, with the ability to prioritise and manage competing demands
• Hold a Level 3 or Level 4 Information, Advice and Guidance (IAG) qualification, or be willing to work towards this
Whilst we welcome applications from those with lived experience, this role requires an enhanced DBS check and HMPPS EL1 vetting. Due to the time required to complete these checks, successful candidates will be offered a start date at least 6 weeks from the point of job offer. This should allow sufficient time for all necessary pre-employment clearances to be obtained
Our Justice division is dedicated to transforming lives and creating safer communities. Our mission is to reduce reoffending, build stronger communities, and help people realise their potential.

Additional Information
At Ingeus, we’ve spent time listening to our employees to build our benefits package;
• 25 days of annual leave plus bank holidays, with the option to trade for additional leave.
• EAP Support programme available 24/7, including 6 free counselling sessions.
• Private medical insurance and life assurance.
• Up to 2 days of Community Giving (volunteering) each year to support a cause that matters to you.
• Eyecare vouchers to help with glasses or eye care.
• Online Shopping discounts
• Cycle to Work scheme and travel season ticket loan.
• Long service awards to celebrate your commitment.
• Salary Finance offering financial education and advice.
• The opportunity to purchase extra benefits like critical illness cover and dental insurance.

If you require any support or adjustments—whether that’s help with the application, interview format, or anything else—we’re here to listen and work with you to find the best approach.
Our goal is to ensure you can showcase your skills and potential in a way that works for you. Please don’t hesitate to contact us at careers@ingeus.co.uk to discuss how we can support you
If you think you have what it takes, don't delay and apply today – We may shortlist and conduct interviews before the closing date and if we receive enough applications this role may close early.

About This Job
Asset‑intensive organisations are under increasing pressure to improve the performance of their operational technology and asset systems, driven by rising customer and regulatory expectations and the growing complexity of digitally enabled infrastructure. Many are at different stages of asset‑management maturity, from establishing foundational practices to pushing the boundaries of innovation. PA helps clients navigate this challenge by strengthening their asset‑management capabilities, modernising lifecycle approaches, and delivering measurable improvements across cost, risk and service performance, creating exciting, varied work for consultants at the intersection of OT, asset management and transformation.
About the role
We are looking for exceptional Consultants and Senior Consultants to join our growing Asset Management practice, with a particular focus on Operational Technology (OT) across the UK transport sector. Our clients, including major national infrastructure operators, are increasingly seeking support to improve the performance of operational technology, strengthen management of critical assets, and modernise how maintenance, renewal and operational decision‑making are carried out. You will work with organisations that own and operate complex, safety‑critical and highly regulated infrastructure. Your role will help clients improve the performance of their OpTech environments, make better use of asset data, and implement more effective approaches to maintaining and renewing their assets.
What you will do
Improve the performance of OT and asset systems
• Diagnose how OT assets and operational systems are maintained, monitored and renewed.
• Identify opportunities to improve the performance of OT systems, increasing reliability, resilience and availability.
• Strengthen maintenance, inspection and renewal approaches using risk‑based, proactive AM practices.
Strengthen asset‑management maturity across the lifecycle
• Apply ISO 55001‑aligned asset‑management principles to clarify roles, responsibilities, asset strategies and lifecycle controls.
• Support the development of asset‑management system elements such as governance, standards, assurance and continuous improvement.
• Shape lifecycle approaches (plan – design – deliver – operate – renew) that drive consistent performance.
Analyse performance, risk and operational insight
• Use operational data, fault/incident logs, service KPIs and asset health information to identify root causes of underperformance.
• Build baselines of asset & OT performance to inform investment cases and improvement plans.
• Recommend actions that improve the performance, reliability and sustainability of OT estates.
Support transformation and delivery
• Contribute to operating‑model improvements, new ways of working, and improved governance structures.
• Help clients adopt digital tools, telemetry, monitoring platforms and analytics to enhance lifecycle decision‑making.
• Support delivery of improvement roadmaps, business cases and change artefacts.
Hybrid working - our approach is to be in the office or on client site a minimum of 2 days per week. However, the actual time you spend and where you spend it will vary by role or assignment, including up to 5 days per week on a client site.

Qualifications
Experience (one or more of the following):
• Exposure to operational technology environments (control rooms, SCADA‑linked assets, roadside systems, industrial automation, etc.).
• Experience in engineering, maintenance, operations, reliability engineering, systems engineering or infrastructure management.
• Experience in asset‑management roles covering asset strategies, lifecycle planning, performance management or investment planning.
• Experience working with operational or performance data.
• Strong analytical and structured problem‑solving skills.
• Ability to translate operational issues into business implications (performance, cost, risk, safety).
• Clear communication and stakeholder engagement abilities.
• Curiosity and appetite to develop deeper expertise in asset management and OT.
Qualifications
You are likely to have one or more of the following (or be keen to develop them):
Asset‑Management Frameworks
• Understanding of ISO 55001 and modern asset‑management system principles.
• Knowledge of lifecycle asset management, risk‑based maintenance, reliability engineering or asset‑investment planning.
• Awareness of asset‑management maturity models.
• Membership (or interest in membership) of professional bodies such as IAM.
Operational Technology & Engineering
• Exposure to OT environments such as SCADA, PLCs, roadside or field assets, control systems, telemetry, signalling or industrial OT.
• Understanding of how OT assets degrade, fail, are maintained and renewed.
Desirable (but not required)
• Experience with asset‑performance monitoring tools or APM platforms.
• Familiarity with operational risk, safety or assurance frameworks.
• Understanding of the interfaces between OT, IT, operations and engineering.
Why join us?
• Shape solutions that improve the performance of critical infrastructure and OT systems.
• Learn from and work alongside specialists in asset management, OT, engineering, data and operations.
• Build a career across asset strategy, lifecycle optimisation, performance improvement and operating‑model design.
• Work in a supportive, multidisciplinary team delivering meaningful change for clients.
We know the skill-gap and ‘somewhat need to tick every box’ can get in the way of meeting brilliant candidates, so please don’t hesitate to apply – we’d love to hear from you.
Apply today by completing our online application
Please be aware that some of our UK roles at PA Consulting require a UK security clearance.
All PA people are required to undergo background checks and to achieve the Baseline Personnel Security Standard however, some UK roles also require higher levels of National Security Vetting, where applicants must have at least 5 years of continuous residency in the UK.
We therefore ask that you only apply if you meet the residency requirements (i.e. you are a British citizen or have been resident in the UK for the past 5 years), as this is the prerequisite for a security clearance. If you're unsure about your eligibility, we encourage you to review the UK Government’s guidance on security vetting before applying.

Life At PA encompasses our peoples' experience at PA. It's about how we enrich peoples’ working lives by giving them access to unique people and growth opportunities and purpose led meaningful work.

jobs.smartrecruiters.com/wise/7440001552.description_excerpt:
About This Job
The role
We’re looking for a Senior Product Analytics Manager to set the strategic direction for analytics in our Global Send Experience Squad. You’ll help the squad decide where to focus, which customer problems to solve and how Wise can grow its global money transfer business, which today drives 5% of all cross-border transfers in the world for personal customers.
You’ll work closely with Product, Design and Engineering to lead discovery across the remittance space: building a deep understanding of customer needs, finding the biggest opportunities and turning them into a clear product strategy. You’ll influence decisions across the factors that shape whether customers choose to send money with Wise—including price, speed and convenience—throughout the whole customer lifecycle, from a customer’s first transfer to the choices they make as a returning customer.
You’ll lead a group of senior analysts. Your focus will be on setting the team’s direction and helping the squad make its most important strategic decisions. You’ll coach analysts to partner closely with teams on day-to-day product questions, while staying hands-on with the most complex and consequential opportunities yourself.
You’ll help us answer questions such as:
•
Where are the biggest opportunities to grow money transfers around the world?
•
What matters most to customers when they decide where, when and how to send money?
•
How do price, speed and convenience shape customers’ choices and behaviour?
•
How could an AI-powered concierge help customers find and complete the right transfer, while making the experience simpler and more personal?
•
How can we make the experience work better for both new and returning customers?
•
Which customer problems should we solve to make the biggest difference to growth and customer value?
•
How should we focus our product strategy to grow our money transfer revenues 10x over the next few years?
What you’ll be doing
•
Set the strategic direction for the squad. Partner with Product, Design and Engineering to build a clear view of customer needs, market opportunities and the choices Wise should make next.
•
Lead discovery and opportunity finding. Explore customer behaviour and the end-to-end transfer journey to identify unmet needs, friction and growth opportunities. Help the squad understand not just what is happening, but where it has the greatest opportunity to act.
•
Influence the whole customer decision. Bring an analytical perspective to how customers weigh price, speed and convenience when choosing how to send money, across both new and returning customer journeys.
•
Turn opportunities into product priorities. Size customer and commercial opportunities, develop clear points of view and help teams make focused, evidence-based choices about what to build and why.
•
Lead and develop a group of senior analysts. Set a high bar for analytical thinking and impact, coach analysts in their work and careers, and create the conditions for them to support their teams effectively.
•
Enable strong day-to-day squad decisions. Coach analysts to work closely with their product teams, bring useful insights into planning and discovery, and help teams learn from product changes and customer behaviour.
•
Stay hands-on with the most important problems. Work directly on high-impact or ambiguous questions, and guide the team through complex analysis when the strategic stakes are high.
•
Bring people together around a shared view. Communicate complex evidence clearly, influence senior stakeholders and help cross-functional teams turn strategic choices into action.

Qualifications
What you’ll bring
•
Experience leading and developing strong analytics teams, including experienced or senior analysts.
•
A track record of shaping product strategy and business direction through analytics.
•
Strong product and commercial judgement: you can connect customer needs, product choices, growth and sustainable economics.
•
Experience leading discovery and identifying high-value opportunities in ambiguous problem spaces.
•
A deep understanding of product analytics and customer behaviour across acquisition, conversion and retention.
•
Expertise in using quantitative evidence—including experimentation and causal analysis—to inform decisions, while knowing when the most valuable contribution is defining the right problem or opportunity.
•
Strong technical analytical skills, including SQL, and the ability to guide reliable, high-quality analytics.
•
Excellent communication skills: you can make complex ideas clear, form a point of view and bring people with you.
•
The ability to set long-term direction while staying close enough to the work to help teams make progress.
•
An interest in international payments and the needs of people sending money across borders.
How you’ll work
You’ll be a strategic partner to the Global Send Experience Squad, working closely with Product, Design and Engineering to understand the space, find opportunities and shape what the squad does next.
You’ll lead a team of senior analysts who work alongside their product teams on day-to-day questions and decisions. You’ll help them connect that work to the squad’s broader strategy, share insights across teams and keep the focus on the customer and business outcomes that matter most.
Why this role matters
Sending money across borders is at the heart of Wise. By helping us understand what customers need and setting a clear direction for how we serve them, you’ll shape the choices that make Wise the best way to send money—at every stage of the customer journey.
You’ll help us grow our money transfer business while making it easier, faster and more affordable for customers around the world. For everyone, everywhere.
​​​​​​

Additional Information
What do we offer:
•
Salary: £105,000 - £150,000
•
Company Restricted Stock Units
•
Numerous great benefits in our London office
Key benefits:
•
Hybrid working
•
Paid annual holiday, sick days, parental leave and other leave opportunities
•
6 weeks of paid sabbatical after 4 years at Wise on top of annual leave
For everyone, everywhere. We're people building money without borders  — without judgement or prejudice, too. We believe teams are strongest when they are diverse, equitable and inclusive.
We're proud to have a truly international team, and we celebrate our differences.
Inclusive teams help us live our values and make sure every Wiser feels respected, empowered to contribute towards our mission and able to progress in their careers.
If you want to find out more about what it's like to work at Wise visit Wise.Jobs.
Keep up to date with life at Wise by following us on LinkedIn and Instagram.

About This Job
About us:
Applications are invited for the role of Head of Hard FM within the Estates Department of the University of the West of England.
Based at our Frenchay campus but covering the entire university estate (predominantly the Bristol area), you will be responsible for all aspects of hard FM for all university properties.
As a member of the Estates senior management team, the successful applicant will lead and manage professional services, support strategic planning and in order to support the efficient managing of the university estate be responsible for operational delivery for all major and specialist contracts and operations.
This post will develop and manage systems of work for sourcing, specifying and scheduling planned and reactive maintenance across the University estate. The post holder manages capital projects linked to the Estates Capital Maintenance (ECM) Plan.
About you:
The skills and experience required for this post are; leadership and operational management of the Hard FM Services (HFMS) team, ability to deliver effective and efficient use of allocated resources, including staffing and R&M and ECM budgets, an effective communicator acting as the key liaison point for the HFMS team with other services and faculties, and a keen facilitator of collaborative working and developing the service.
Furthermore, lead and contribute to University wide projects, developing and promoting innovative thinking and being a strategic thinker to contribute to the development of University policies and procedures in line with service strategy and plans.
About UWE Bristol:
We are one of the largest providers of Higher Education in the South West with over 30,000 students, 250,000 alumni and 3,800 staff. We are both globally connected and regionally embedded, with strong employer and partner connections. Our staff and students come from over 160 countries making this a diverse, dynamic and rewarding place to work and study.
We are an ambitious university. Together, our people are working hard to advance knowledge, inspire people and transform futures. We are looking for people with the skills and ambition to help us achieve those aims.
We have a lot to be proud of at UWE, our achievements include an impressive 88% overall student satisfaction in the most recent National Student Satisfaction survey, placing us 2nd of all universities in England and 7th in the UK. We are 6th in the UK for postgraduate student satisfaction (Postgraduate Taught Experience Survey) and importantly, 96% of UWE Bristol graduates are in employment or further study within six months after graduation. We have also achieved TEF Gold status, have been ranked 21st in The Guardian Best UK Universities 2021 and 29th in the latest Times Higher Education 'Table of Tables'.
This post is based at our lively Frenchay campus where we have invested in the latest facilities and resources to give both our staff and students access to everything they need to succeed – with £300m having been invested recently on new state-of-the-art learning spaces and accommodation while incredible new facilities continue to be developed to enhance our offer even further.
Frenchay campus has excellent transport links; as well as being located near the motorway network we are within walking distance of two train stations, our bus terminus connects us to the local bus and metrobus network and we also have a range of cycling and changing facilities, making our campus the ideal place to work for those commuting to Bristol.
In addition to progressive pay rates, UWE Bristol offers a wide range of employee benefits including:
• a generous holiday allowance of 27 days
• up to 12.5 bank holiday/closure days per year
• flexible working
• excellent defined benefit pension schemes
• access to employee assistance programme
• ongoing learning and development opportunities
• family friendly policies and wellbeing initiatives
• onsite nursery at our Frenchay Campus.
• savings on purchases via Wider Wallet scheme
• option to participate in the cycle to work scheme
Further information
This is a permanent post, and is full-time working 37 hours per week. This post is not available on a jobshare basis.
We particularly encourage applications from BAME applicants as we are currently under represented in these areas - although all appointments will be made on merit.
The University’s normal practice is that new appointments will be made at the starting point of the grade.
UWE is committed to supporting and promoting equality and diversity to create an inclusive working environment. We believe this can be achieved through attracting, developing, and retaining a diverse range of staff from many different backgrounds who share our ambition to be a university recognised for the success and impact of our practice-oriented programmes; our strong industry networks and our inclusive global outlook.
We are able to sponsor qualifying candidates for this role under the Home Office Skilled Worker visa route. Please read our Skilled Worker Guidance to assess if you will be eligible to be sponsored under the criteria.
Please also refer to the Home Office Right to Work Checklist which provides details of which documents are acceptable to prove your right to work in the UK. Should you be shortlisted you will be asked to produce your right to work documents at your interview.

About This Job
Your Responsibilities
From day one, you’ll work with real project and cost information while learning how commercial teams support successful project delivery. You’ll help produce clear, accurate analysis, contribute to commercial management, cost verification and auditing activities and develop your understanding of contracts, project controls and commercial management.
Your main responsibilities include:
•
▪ Supporting cost planning, cost management and commercial reporting activities.
▪ Assisting with procurement support and contract administration.
▪ Contributing to measurement, quantification, cost verification and audit activities.
▪ Collating and analysing project and cost information to support reporting and decision making.
▪ Helping prepare clear, accurate and professionally presented reports, analysis and commercial documentation.
▪ Supporting financial and schedule tracking across projects and programmes.
▪ Identifying risks, issues or changes and escalating them to senior team members where appropriate.
▪ Working with colleagues and stakeholders across multidisciplinary project teams.
Why Join Us?
🚀 Give purpose to your career by joining a company that contributes sustainably to the production of low-carbon, competitive, and sovereign energy.
🌍 Explore a wide variety of projects and careers within a strong group, ensuring stimulating and diverse assignments throughout your career.
📚 Develop your skills through an ambitious training program: 5,000 employees trained and more than 100,000 training hours delivered each year.

Qualifications
Your Strengths and Requirements for Success
We’re looking for graduates who:
• Have recently completed, or expect to complete, a degree in Quantity Surveying, Commercial Management, Engineering or a closely related discipline before joining the Graduate Programme.
• Are interested in building a career in commercial management, cost management or auditing.
• Enjoy working with numbers, data and detailed project information.
• Can analyse information and present findings clearly and accurately.
• Have strong organisational skills and feel comfortable working to deadlines.
• Communicate clearly and enjoy working with colleagues and stakeholders.
• Are curious, reliable and willing to ask questions and learn from experienced team members.
An interest in working towards membership of a relevant professional body, such as RICS, CICES or CIOB, would also be beneficial.

Additional Information
Eligibility Requirements:
To join our Graduate Scheme, you must be a UK sole national and a UK resident, as this is required for the type of work we do. You’ll also need to be able to obtain a minimum of Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) clearance, with some roles requiring higher levels of clearance.
As part of the programme, you should also be willing to relocate or travel within the UK, and we’ll provide relocation support where needed.
More information on the security vetting process and clearance levels can be found on the UK Government website: National Security Vetting: clearance levels
Recruitment Process
After submitting your application, you’ll receive confirmation of next steps. If successful at screening, one of our recruitment team will call you to discuss:
📄 Your application and eligibility
⚡ Your passion for energy transformation
🎓 Your interest in and knowledge of your chosen discipline
Successful applicants will then be invited to attend an in-person assessment centre at one of our UK offices.
NOTICE TO CANDIDATES ON RECRUITMENT FRAUD - We are committed to safeguarding candidates from fraudulent activity associated with our recruitment process. Please note that we will never offer specialist CV writing services, request payment or ask for sensitive personal information during the recruitment process.
We are committed to equal treatment of candidates and promote, as well as foster all forms of diversity within our company. We believe that bringing together people with different backgrounds and perspectives is essential for creating innovative and impactful solutions. Skills, talent, and our people’s ability to dare are the only things that matter !. Bring your unique contributions and help us shape the future.

About This Job
We are seeking an experienced CMM Programmer & Metrology Engineer to support precision measurement, inspection, and quality assurance activities within a highly regulated manufacturing environment. The successful candidate will be responsible for developing and validating CMM programs, performing measurement system analysis, supporting production and engineering teams, and driving continuous improvement initiatives to ensure product quality and process capability.
This is an excellent opportunity for a proactive and technically skilled professional who enjoys combining hands-on metrology expertise with problem-solving and process improvement activities.
• Location: Gloucester
• On Site: Fully Onsite

• Analyse measurement results and support investigations into dimensional or quality-related issues.
• Work closely with Manufacturing, Quality, and Engineering teams to resolve inspection and process challenges.
• Support root cause investigations and implement corrective actions to improve product quality.
• Ensure measurement processes comply with quality standards and company procedures.
• Drive continuous improvement initiatives relating to metrology, inspection efficiency, and process capability.
• Maintain inspection documentation, records, and measurement reports.
• Provide technical support and guidance on dimensional measurement best practices.
• Support the introduction of new products and manufacturing processes from a metrology perspective.

• Strong experience programming and validating Coordinate Measuring Machines (CMM).
• Mandatory: Proven knowledge and practical experience using MODUS software.
• Experience conducting and interpreting Gauge R&R and Measurement System Analysis (MSA) studies.
• Ability to read and interpret complex engineering drawings and technical specifications.
• Strong understanding of Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T).
• Experience supporting quality, inspection, or manufacturing activities within a regulated engineering environment.
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with experience conducting root cause investigations.
• Excellent attention to detail and commitment to quality standards.
• Ability to work independently and manage priorities with minimal supervision.
• Strong communication skills and ability to collaborate with both engineering and production teams.
Required Qualifications:
• A Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Engineering, or equivalent military experience.
Desirable Skills:
• Strong experience programming and validating Coordinate Measuring Machines (CMM).
• Proven knowledge and practical experience using MODUS software.
• Experience conducting and interpreting Gauge R&R and Measurement System Analysis (MSA) studies.
• Ability to read and interpret complex engineering drawings and technical specifications.

About This Job
Due to increased opportunities and demand in the Energy & Natural Resources division, the Energy & Natural Resources team are recruiting a Senior Project Planner to join a diverse and supportive team during a period of significant growth. Our nuclear client is at the forefront of industry leading change, and we are keen to speak to individuals with project planning experience to see what Turner & Townsend can offer you. Candidates will be required to be present in our client office for 3 days per week.
MAIN PURPOSE OF ROLE
A Planner will be responsible for work packages and projects of varying size and complexity. Due to the nature of the programme of works, work packages may vary in size with Planners accountable for scheduling multiple smaller projects or one which could be significantly larger in value. A Planner will be responsible for taking the lead on planning for multiple non-related projects or single highly complex projects within the programme of works. They will understand and manage relationships between time, cost, risk, change, reporting and scope, with accountability for creating and maintaining robust schedules that provide our clients with accurate data to drive management decisions. They will play a key role in ensuring that client objectives are met and that projects are delivered to time and cost targets and the appropriate quality standards.
KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES
• As a Planner, you have a passion to provide services as required by our clients, which may include:
• Taking the lead on planning, supporting more junior planning professionals on novel, high value projects or programmes.
• Creation, development and maintenance of project schedules that assist and align with project requirements on a complex, risk managed project or programme.
• Adherence to NEC or FIDIC contract processes for management of schedule data and submissions.
• Assisting the project team to develop status reports to keep management informed on project progress.
• Involvement with senior team in oversight of day-to-day management, staffing and the implementation of Integrated Project Controls standards and processes.
• Reducing uncertainty, improving efficiency and understanding project objectives.
• Interacting with the project team to define scope of work to develop and update detailed schedules, cost information and identification of variances from original schedule.
• Assisting project managers to schedule work and coordinate assignments.
• Evaluation of project schedule progress and performance and identify developing problem areas.
• Analysis of float, critical path and constraints to understand the effect of approved changes or slippages to schedule, recommending alternative courses of action for recovery.
• Undertaking project progress reviews.
• Monitoring and consolidation of multiple project schedules into Integrated master Schedule (IMS).
• Monitoring the project managers reporting system summarising the progress status of all projects.
• Monitor and advise on status of project KPIs across multiple projects.
• Understand and report EVM on a periodic basis.
• Functional management of planning personnel within the Turner & Townsend team, conducting mentoring and coaching as required.

Qualifications
You have professional Project Controls experience specialising in Planning & Scheduling in one or more sectors across the whole Project lifecycle. While nuclear experience is desirable it is not an absolute requirement. You have strong knowledge and proficiency with Primavera (P6) and other planning and resourcing software and can coordinate and work with other teams utilising your multi-disciplinary knowledge.
You will be a strong communicator, able to demonstrate leadership behaviours with the ability to influence, manage, motivate, coach and develop a team by fostering a diverse and inclusive environment. You promote empowerment and contribution and have a passion to build a community and support network beyond your delivery role.
You also;
• Will be able to obtain BPSS level security clearance.
• Are a member of a relevant professional body e.g., Association for Project Management, Project Management Institute.
• Have excellent verbal and written communication skills.
• Have the ability to make risk-based decisions where the parameters are unclear, and judgement is needed.
• Have strong leadership skills with the ability to mobilise, inspire and lead by example.
• Have strong stakeholder management experience.
• Can navigate through conflict situations and defuse tension.
• Have a desire to work within the nuclear sector.

Our inspired people share our vision and mission. We provide a great place to work, where each person has the opportunity and voice to affect change.
We want our people to succeed both in work and life. To support this we promote a healthy, productive and flexible working environment that respects work-life balance.

About This Job
At SIXT, our fleet is our business. As our new Fleet Utilisation & Rotation Professional, you'll own fleet utilisation across the UK Van & Truck business, making sure every vehicle is in the right place at the right time to maximise availability and commercial performance. Using data driven insights, you'll work cross functionally with Commercial, Operations, Sales and Fleet Administration to optimise asset utilisation, improve revenue and support business growth. Drive Fleet Utilisation You own fleet utilisation performance across the UK Van & Truck network, monitoring trends to increase revenue and reduce idle time, producing regular reporting with actionable commercial insights, partnering with branch and operational teams to maximise availability, and developing initiatives that improve overall fleet performance
Lead Fleet Deployment & Rotation You own the allocation strategy for all new vehicles entering the fleet, ensuring they're deployed where they generate the greatest commercial return, coordinating vehicle movements to respond quickly to customer demand and operational requirements, and supporting fleet expansion and network growth through effective deployment planning
Support Fleet Planning You analyse utilisation, booking trends and demand forecasts, provide recommendations to support fleet ordering and investment decisions, identify future capacity constraints and commercial opportunities, and help optimise fleet mix across locations to maximise return on assets
Improve Fleet Availability You monitor all out of service vehicles across the network, work closely with Operations, suppliers and workshops to minimise downtime, identify recurring issues affecting availability and drive root cause solutions, and improve fleet readiness so customers always have access to the vehicles they need
Build Strong Business Partnerships You develop effective relationships across internal and external teams, act as the central point of coordination for fleet deployment decisions, present utilisation and performance updates to senior stakeholders, and influence decision making through clear analysis and commercial recommendations
Drive Continuous Improvement You challenge existing processes to find smarter ways of working, support automation, reporting enhancements and improved data visibility, and strengthen governance and controls throughout the fleet lifecycle while contributing to strategic commercial and operational improvement projects
Success Metrics You're measured on tangible commercial outcomes, including fleet utilisation performance, reduction in vehicle idle days, revenue per vehicle or category, speed of new vehicle deployment, allocation lead times and fleet rotation effectiveness
YOUR SKILLS MATTER
• Fleet Expertise You bring experience within fleet, vehicle rental, logistics, transport or commercial operations, ideally including vehicle rental or fleet management, knowledge of fleet management systems, Prohire or Business Intelligence tools, and an understanding of vehicle lifecycle management
• Analytical & Commercial Insight You have strong analytical skills with advanced Excel capability, the ability to interpret complex data and translate it into commercial actions, and solid commercial awareness of fleet utilisation and asset management, always prioritising what matters most to drive performance
• Planning & Organisation You bring excellent planning and organisational skills, keeping fleet decisions structured and on track
• Stakeholder Management You have strong stakeholder management and communication skills, building trusted relationships and collaborating across departments to achieve the best outcomes for the business
• Continuous Improvement You enjoy delivering process improvement or transformation initiatives, challenging the status quo, embracing innovation, and addressing root causes rather than symptoms to proactively remove barriers to success
• Ownership You take accountability for fleet performance, make informed decisions and deliver results, always putting customers at the centre of every fleet decision
WHAT WE OFFER
• Competitive Salary & Financial Security Receive a competitive salary and enrol in SIXT’s pension scheme for long-term security.
• AI at your fingertips From day one, you'll have access to Claude by Anthropic and SIXTgpt, SIXT's own AI platform, to supercharge your work. We invest in every team member's AI journey: encouraging experimentation, building knowledge, and making sure you're ahead of the curve
• Generous Time Off Enjoy 22 days of annual leave plus bank holidays
• Training & Development Benefit from paid training sessions and various development opportunities
• Exclusive Employee Benefits Access special terms for SIXT car hire and extend these perks to friends and family through our staff rental scheme
• Health, Wellbeing & Life Assurance Utilize the Medicash health cashback plan and the Yulife wellbeing app, along with in-service life assurance
• Family-Friendly Support & Assistance Enjoy generous family-friendly provisions and access our Employee Assistance Programme for additional support

About This Job
Our functional specialists write reports which help the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) make important decisions about a person’s health and care.
Maybe you’re a nurse right now and you’d like to move away from direct care - this role offers you the chance to not only improve your assessment skills, but also to use your knowledge and experience to make important clinical recommendations. Or you might be an occupational therapist, physiotherapist or paramedic wanting to learn how to evaluate situations in a different way in a different setting. We’re looking for people with the compassion and experience to understand our claimants’ health conditions/disabilities and how they impact their lives.
This role is different from other healthcare professions, and that’s why we take your training and development seriously. You’ll receive comprehensive training with time set aside for self-development learning.
If you’re looking for a change, including more regular working hours, a competitive salary and are ready to expand your skills and experience, this could be the role for you.
What you’ll do in this role:
• Conduct functional assessments which include initial reviews, face-to-face, video or telephone assessments to evaluate how a claimant’s health condition or disability affects them for various types of benefit.
• Analyse and interpret clinical information and supporting evidence.
• Write detailed evidence-based reports to support the DWP/DfC in making informed and objective decisions - no treatment or diagnosis required.
• Use IT systems to support clinical decision-making and report writing.
• Develop your clinical knowledge and constantly learn about health conditions which are less familiar to you.
• This role will deliver mainly face-to-face assessments.
What are PIP and WCA?
• Personal Independence Payment (PIP) is a benefit for people with a long-term health condition or impairment. It is paid to make a contribution to the extra costs that disabled people may face, to help them lead full, active and independent lives.
• Work Capability Assessment (WCA) is a functional assessment that looks at a range of different activities relating to physical, mental, intellectual and cognitive functions, to help DWP determine a customer's capability for work or work-related activity.

Qualifications

• one year's post-registration experience as a nurse (RMN, RNLD, RGN), occupational therapist, physiotherapist or paramedic

• excellent observational and communication skills, giving you the ability to listen, empathise and dig deeper

• solid experience with using IT and Microsoft Office, as well as remotely accessing systems
• a current valid driving licence or access to a form of transport to attend your nearest assessment centre

At vetting, you will undergo an enhanced criminality check which will show both spent and unspent convictions.

Please note for part-time roles the initial training period of 8 weeks (paid) is full time so candidate must be able to commit to that.

jobs.smartrecruiters.com/syngentagroup/7.description_excerpt:
About This Job
At Syngenta, our goal is to build the most collaborative and trustworthy team in agriculture, providing top-quality seeds and innovative crop protection solutions that improve farmers' success. To support this mission, Syngenta’s Hiring Team is seeking an Onsite Engineering Planner in Huddersfield, UK.
Role Overview
Responsible for planning, scoping, and delivering detailed work packages for routine maintenance and planned outages across electrical, instrumentation, mechanical, and civil disciplines. The role requires regular attendance at the job face to gather accurate, first-hand information that underpins well-defined and executable job scopes. Acting as the key link between engineering, operations, and contractors, the post holder ensures all activities are fully scoped, resourced ahead of scheduling, scheduled, and aligned with site safety and production requirements.
Key responsibilities
• Attend the job face across electrical, instrumentation, mechanical, and civil disciplines to gather first-hand information and develop accurate, complete job scopes.
• Prepare detailed work packages including task sequences, resource plans, materials, drawings, isolation plans, risk assessments, and permit requirements.
• Build and maintain master plan for routine maintenance (3-month rolling schedule) and planned outages, identifying critical path activities and cross-functional dependencies.
• Coordinate with Asset Engineers, Operations, Project teams, and Contractors to integrate maintenance, cleanout, and commissioning activities through to execution.
• Manage CMMS data (SAP), maintaining accurate work orders, task lists, equipment histories, and resource requirements.
• Lead weekly scheduling meetings and report on schedule adherence, critical paths, and resource utilisation.
• Liaise with stores and procurement to ensure parts, consumables, and specialist tools are available ahead of scheduled work.
• Review job plans post-execution, driving continuous improvement in planning quality and contributing to reliability programmes.

Qualifications
• Minimum 5 years’ experience in maintenance planning or engineering within chemical manufacturing, petrochemical, oil & gas, pharmaceutical, or a heavy process industry.
• Proven experience planning across at least two of the following disciplines: electrical, instrumentation, mechanical, or civil engineering.
• Demonstrated experience in shutdown, turnaround, or outage planning, including the development of detailed job lists, execution schedules, and work packages.
• Proven proficiency in CMMS systems, specifically SAP Plant Maintenance, including work order management, equipment history, and task list maintenance.
• Strong working knowledge of scheduling methodologies and tools (e.g. Microsoft Project, Primavera P6, Prometheus).
• Familiarity with engineering documentation such as P&IDs, equipment drawings, and specifications.
• Knowledge of permit-to-work systems, risk assessment processes, and site safety procedures.
• Experience in stakeholder management across multiple functions
• Highly organised, able to manage multiple scopes simultaneously under time pressure.
• HNC/HND in a relevant engineering discipline, or equivalent demonstrable experience.

Additional Information
At the Huddersfield Manufacturing Centre we make important Crop Protection products that are used in over 120 countries worldwide. These products help our growers to meet the ever-increasing demand for food, feed and fuel, and our talented & dedicated teams make this possible. The Huddersfield team is proactive, driven, and friendly, with a strong emphasis on diversity, equality and inclusion. We work cross functionally to get the job done!
What We Offer
• A culture that celebrates diversity & inclusion, promotes professional development, and strives for a work-life balance that supports the team members.
• Extensive benefits package including a generous pension scheme, bonus scheme, private medical & life insurance.
• Up to 31.5 days annual holiday plus 8 UK bank holidays.
• 36-hour working week.
Syngenta is an Equal Opportunity Employer and does not discriminate in recruitment, hiring, training, promotion or any other employment practices for reasons of race, color, religion, gender, national origin, age, sexual orientation, marital or veteran status, disability, or any other legally protected status.

Equal to your technical work, you will also develop as a consultant. This means harnessing your entrepreneurial mindset: building an understanding of the markets we work in, engaging directly with clients to present your findings, and proactively ensuring their requirements are fully understood and met. As you gain experience, you will have opportunities to lead projects, build teams, and manage client relationships. What are PIP and WCA?
• Personal Independence Payment (PIP) is a benefit for people with a long-term health condition or impairment. It is paid to make a contribution to the extra costs that disabled people may face, to help them lead full, active and independent lives.
• Work Capability Assessment (WCA) is a functional assessment that looks at a range of different activities relating to physical, mental, intellectual and cognitive functions, to help DWP determine a customer's capability for work or work-related activity.

Qualifications

• NMC registered Nurse (RGN, RMN or RNLD) or HCPC registered paramedic, occupational therapist or physiotherapist with a valid PIN and no current restrictions

• Comfortable working quickly to meet structured targets.
• Good IT skills including Microsoft Office, and the ability to learn new systems while working remotely.
• excellent observational and communication skills, giving you the ability to listen, empathise and dig deeper.

About This Job
Position Summary
Under the direction of the Head of Quality Risk Assessment and Combination Products within Integrated Medical Quality and Device Safety, Global Patient Safety, the Senior Medical Director, serves as a trusted strategic partner, providing medical quality and device safety expertise to cross-enterprise stakeholders. The scope of responsibility spans the entire AbbVie portfolio, with consultation and accountability that may include product complaints, surveillance, quality risk management and device risk management.  The Senior Medical Director is a recognized medical and scientific expert who will work closely with Global Patient Safety (GPS) Therapeutic Area stakeholders to support pipeline enablement and strategic development activities for priority pipeline assets, with responsibility for leading the assessment and management of medical device safety signals, product quality issues, and emerging risks, while providing strategic guidance on benefit-risk evaluations and risk mitigation activities. The role drives proactive identification, interpretation, communication, and mitigation of safety concerns while ensuring alignment with global regulatory requirements and AbbVie's patient safety objectives.
Key Responsibilities
Signal Detection and Risk Assessment
• Perform medical assessment of product complaints, adverse events, and product quality issues to determine potential patient impact, reportability, and need for escalation.
• Lead evaluation of safety signals, adverse event trends, and emerging risks from post-market surveillance, literature, clinical studies, and other data sources.
• Contribute to and review Post-Market Surveillance System (PMSS) and Post-Market Clinical Follow-Up (PMCF) activities, ensuring integration of safety data into ongoing benefit-risk assessments.
Medical Quality and Device Safety & Risk Management
• Provide medical expertise for Quality Risk Management (QRM) activities, including benefit-risk evaluations, risk mitigation plans, and cross-functional risk reviews.
• Serve as a medical safety expert accountable for Health Hazard Assessments (HHA) for quality and device-related issues.
• Provide medical input and oversight for Device Risk Management activities throughout the product lifecycle, ensuring risks are appropriately identified, evaluated, monitored and controlled.
• Author, review, and contribute to regulatory submissions, health authority responses, deficiency responses, and other regulatory communications related to device safety, product quality, and risk management.
• Support internal and external inspections, audits, and health authority interactions by serving as a subject matter expert for medical device safety, vigilance, and risk management activities.
Cross-Functional Partnership
• Support process improvement initiatives, procedural development, and implementation of best practices to enhance device safety, surveillance, and quality-related processes.
.

Qualifications
Required Qualifications
• MD, DO, or equivalent medical degree with specialty residency and minimum 2 years of patient management experience required.
• Minimum of 3 to 5 years of experience in drug safety, medical device safety, clinical development, pharmacovigilance, regulatory science, or related functions.
• Strong understanding of global medical device regulations, including FDA, EU MDR, and other international requirements.
• Experience evaluating complex safety signals and contributing to cross-functional risk assessments.
• Excellent written, verbal, and presentation communication skills.
Preferred Qualifications
• Experience with combination products and connected/digital medical devices.
• Experience supporting regulatory inspections and health authority interactions.
• Advanced understanding of risk management, quality systems, and product lifecycle management
